questions.q: How does a playbook differ from the overall incident response plan?
options: A playbook is a specific, pre-thought-out response sequence for one known scenario type, while the plan covers the general process for any incident
A playbook and the plan are two names for the exact same document
A playbook only applies to incidents that have already been fully resolved
A playbook replaces the need for any severity classification
questions.explain: The plan handles incidents generally; a playbook goes a level deeper for one known scenario, with the reasoning done in advance.

questions.q: Why does a ransomware playbook specify isolating affected hosts WITHOUT powering them off?
options: Powering off can destroy memory-resident evidence and, in some cases, trigger further encryption
Powering off instantly removes the ransomware with no other steps needed
Powered-off hosts automatically notify the ransomware group that they've been detected
It has no effect either way, so the instruction doesn't matter
questions.explain: Isolating from the network while leaving the host powered on preserves evidence that would otherwise be lost.

questions.q: Why does a ransomware playbook include a step to verify backups are intact and isolated BEFORE assuming they're usable?
options: Because that verification step gets skipped constantly under pressure if it isn't explicitly written down
Because backups are never relevant to a ransomware incident
Because verifying backups is only required after the ransom has already been paid
Because all backups are automatically assumed to be encrypted
questions.explain: Under pressure, teams often assume backups are fine without checking -- writing the step down prevents that assumption.

questions.q: Why does a business email compromise (BEC) playbook specifically involve notifying Finance?
options: Because BEC is often financial fraud wearing a technical disguise, and a fraudulent wire transfer may need to be flagged or clawed back quickly
Because Finance is responsible for resetting the compromised mailbox's password
Because BEC incidents never involve any email activity at all
Because notifying Finance has no urgency compared to other steps
questions.explain: An attacker impersonating a compromised employee may initiate a fraudulent wire transfer, which Finance needs to catch fast.

questions.q: Why does an insider threat playbook require looping in HR and Legal before any technical action, unlike an external-attacker scenario?
options: Tipping off the employee too early, or acting without proper authorization, can destroy both the evidence and the organization's legal position
HR and Legal are always the first to detect any insider threat
Insider threats never require any technical investigation at all
There is no real difference between insider and external threat response
questions.explain: Because the subject is an employee with legitimate access, premature or unauthorized action can compromise both evidence and legal standing.
